title: WAL commit-path: widen group-commit window and batch writer flushes
configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a group-commit window on nearly every commit but is too narrow to collect siblings, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces the WAL writer to issue an fsync per write instead of batching; wal_waiting_backends persists at p95=1 with sync_average_ms=0.111ms.
mechanism: The WAL commit path still shows a persistent wal_wait anomaly (wal_waiting_backends p95=1, max=1) with sync_average_ms=0.111ms and write_average_ms=0.020ms, while host_io stall fractions are zero and wal_bytes_per_txn is only 4.34. The bottleneck is sync coalescing, not volume: commit_delay=100us is too short to gather the 5 terminals' commits, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 makes the WAL writer fsync each write. Widening the group-commit window to 500us with commit_siblings=3 lets concurrent committers share one fsync, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) batches background writer flushes. This is the mandatory wal_commit_path bundle; wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay and wal_compression are non-actionable at their safe bounds.
query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.876); reducing commit-path queueing shortens InsertTweet and mixed-transaction stalls, freeing terminal slots for the dominant read path.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps as commit-path fsync coalescing removes residual wal_wait stalls.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 and overall p95 decrease slightly; GetUserTweets p50 unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window plus batched writer flushes coalesce fsyncs, lowering mean sync latency.
Fewer per-commit fsyncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Freed terminal capacity from shorter commit stalls raises completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: If the residual wal_wait is caused by WAL buffer pressure rather than sync coalescing, widening the group-commit window will not reduce sync_average_ms and TPS stays flat.
If commit_delay itself adds fixed latency without collecting siblings, InsertTweet p95 rises while sync_average_ms is unchanged.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves commit_delay=100us (too narrow to collect 5 terminals) and wal_writer_flush_after=0 (per-write fsync). Widening the window to 500us with commit_siblings=3 and batching writer flushes to 256 (2MB) directly targets the persistent wal_wait anomaly without touching the supported predicate-lock gains.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units = 2MB) within safe [0,1024]; batches writer-side WAL flushes instead of per-write fsync.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs

cross_domain_requirements: Keep max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0 from the accepted r009 concurrency action; do not revert.
